newsitem.title: USA: Sales of new homes up in June, inventories low.
newsitem.headline: Sales of new homes up in June, inventories low.

text.p: New-home sales strengthened in June, the Commerce Department said on Wednesday, though from a weaker pace in the three prior months than previously thought.

Sales rose 6.1 percent in June to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 819,000 units after a revised 1 percent rise to 772,000 in May. Previously, the department said May sales had jumped 7.1 percent to a much higher rate of 825,000.
Nonetheless, lean inventories of homes for sale indicated the durability of demand within the housing industry.

Commerce revised down its previous estimates of monthly sales for March and April as well as for May. Still, demand for new homes remained brisk in June, reflected in the lowest level of new homes on the market in nearly four years.
The department said there were 282,000 new homes for sale at the end of June, down from 283,000 in May and the lowest level since 278,000 in July 1993.
That amounted to 4.2 months' worth of supply at June's sales pace, the lowest in 26 years since 4.1 months' worth in July 1971.
June sales were running 11.9 percent above the level a year earlier, in June 1996 when new homes were selling at a rate of 732,000 a year.
Monthly sales increased in every region except the Northeast, where they dropped 21.1 percent in June to 71,000 after a 3.4 percent increase in May.
Midwest sales climbed 7 percent to 153,000 after a 9.2 percent increase in May and in the South sales were up 9.2 percent following a 1.2 percent gain in May.
Sales in the West increased strongly by 12.4 percent to 226,000 in June after a 5.2 percent decline in May.
